children: You bought a Nifty call near 22,700, expecting the bounce to continue. Two sessions later, Nifty is at 22,250, and your position is deep in the red. October has delivered several such swings. Now you face trading’s most uncomfortable question: should you exit, or wait?

Many retail traders choose between two extremes. They sell quickly, then watch the market reverse after hitting their stop. Next time, they hold on. The market keeps falling, and their capital slowly disappears.
There is a third choice: repair the trade.

Trade repair means changing the position instead of closing it immediately or pretending nothing happened. The aim is to reduce the loss and keep a reasonable chance of recovery. It does not mean rescuing every bad trade. It means reshaping the position for the market that exists today.

Once Nifty moves against you, your original view has failed. Start again. Look for fresh support and resistance. You can also study the range suggested by implied volatility, or observe the strikes with the highest Call Open Interest and Put Open Interest. This gives you a realistic area in which Nifty may trade.
The new range becomes your repair plan. Every adjustment must pass one test: if Nifty remains inside this range, will the repaired position lose less than the current one?
Find the Risk Causing the Damage

An option position can suffer from three main risks: price movement, time decay, and changes in volatility. Identify the largest problem before choosing a solution. A repair designed for the wrong risk can make the position worse.

If price movement is hurting a long call, selling a call near the upper edge of the new range may collect premium and cushion the loss. The original call still leaves some benefit if Nifty rebounds sharply.
If the market is moving sideways, time decay is the enemy of a bought option. Selling an option against the position can make time decay work in your favour on the sold leg.
If you sold options and implied volatility rises, premiums can expand even when Nifty barely moves. A long calendar or ratio backspread may add exposure to higher volatility and balance the position.

Two rules matter. Never increase size merely to recover faster. Also, when the market is trending strongly against you, a clean exit may be the best repair. Before changing anything, define your maximum acceptable loss, risk limit, and exit point.

Trade repair cannot save every losing position. Its value is that it replaces panic with a plan. Reassess the range, identify the risk, and hedge that risk. Adjust to today’s market, rather than defending yesterday’s prediction. That discipline helps traders protect capital and stay in the game. Trade repair reshapes risk, limits losses, and preserves recovery potential. A careful repair also protects trading capital from emotional decisions and keeps future opportunities open.
